questions.question: Which NCERT Class 12 edition/reprint is canonical for this project?
questions.why: Class 11 decomposition is bound to a specific reprint. Class 12 must name its own, read from the prelims file rather than a filename, before any section denominator is fixed.
questions.resolution: Reprint 2026-27, read from both prelims. Matches the CBSE 041 syllabus year. Rationalised reformatted edition.

questions.question: Does the current CBSE Class XII syllabus contain required scope with no clear NCERT owner?
questions.why: Class 11 had twelve such entries (the FO-series), and two governance defects came from giving them false NCERT ownership. If Class 12 has an equivalent, the CBSE-only sentinel pattern should be planned in from the start rather than retrofitted.

questions.question: Does Class 12 have formative-only topics, and does the Class 11 policy carry over?
questions.why: Class 11's GD-1 arose from labelling official formative content OPTIONAL_ENRICHMENT. The policy — REQUIRED_CORE means inside official instructional scope regardless of summative assessment — should be re-applied only after Class 12's assessment structure is verified, not assumed.

questions.question: Should the many-to-many unit-to-lesson mapping be carried into Class 12?
questions.why: Class 11 ended with 35 of 90 lessons carrying several units and 26 units spread across several lessons. Whether that is pedagogically sound is precisely what the deferred Wave 1 review would answer. Deferring review does not make the question go away; it means Class 12 decomposition proceeds without that evidence.
questions.blocks: nothing yet — decomposition fixes units, not artifacts; the question arrives at authoring

questions.question: How should the project obtain NCERT and CBSE primary sources when their hosts are unreachable from the build environment?
questions.why: Class 11 sources arrived as session uploads. Class 12 cannot be acquired by the agent directly: ncert.nic.in, epathshala.nic.in and cbseacademic.nic.in all refuse connections here, while unrelated hosts respond normally. Either the owner supplies the files as uploads, as happened for Classes 8 and 11, or the project accepts a documented acquisition route it can actually reach.
questions.blocks: all Class 12 source inspection and decomposition
questions.resolution: 14 of 15 files arrived valid. lemh201.pdf (Chapter 7) is truncated, and the Part I appendices, Answers and Supplementary Material were never part of the 15. Re-download lemh201 and obtain the appendix files from NCERT.
